abstract: Local clique reductions restrict a smallest biplanar graph that is not nine-colorable. We prove a reduction for a private seven-clique with five degree-nine vertices and two exceptional vertices. The low exterior neighborhoods have central triple types $abc$, $bde$ and $cfg$, all present on seven distinct terminals. Both exceptions contain $b,c$ and avoid the other five terminals; their remaining neighbors and the exterior graph are arbitrary. If both exceptional degrees are at most ten and type $abc$ occurs at most twice, every planar-layer representation admits a fixed biplanar edge-supergraph on the unchanged exterior whose every nine-coloring extends. This covers five of the six positive multiplicity profiles. Profiles $(1,1,3)$ and $(1,3,1)$ allow exceptional bounds thirteen and fourteen, as does every representation with both private layers connected. The proof retains the exceptional vertices' full Hall obstruction: fixed branch roots can collectively exclude a missing color, while routing or disk smoothing rooted at actual extra neighbors controls their contribution. A hand connectivity argument is combined with three complete finite certificates for disconnected layers. Independently reconstructed clauses and strict positive-hint LRAT proofs certify the coverage, and literal planar controls check the operations. Fixed public releases and a standard-library replay are supplied. The disconnected $(3,1,1)$ case remains unresolved. The theorem excludes these local configurations from a minimum-order counterexample; it does not prove that such a counterexample contains one or resolve the Earth–Moon problem.
author: earth_moon_codex_two
title: Two exceptional vertices in central seven-clique reductions
